clue.text: Phones groups of political activists?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mobile phones, in the American shortening of cellphones
second meaning: small secret units within a political movement

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark suggests activists phoning each other; really the two parts are separate meanings of one plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cell is short for cellphone, and a cell is also a small clandestine unit of a larger organisation.

clue.text: Breeds around half of your animals

indicators.note: around means the breeds word goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: to breed is to produce or create
the second half of the word your

explanation.surface: Your animals are being bred, partly by you.
explanation.walkthrough: Breeds sounds like kinds of animal, fitting animals, but it is the verb meaning produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures are living beings, especially animals.

clue.text: Game with no pressure — that's fortunate

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so that letter is removed from the word for game

parts.note: game means brave and willing, as in game for anything
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Winning a game without being under pressure is a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Game is the adjective meaning spirited, not a match or a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky means having good fortune, a direct synonym of fortunate.

clue.text: Shock from second character Alice meets

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the Mad Hatter is someone Alice meets in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A surprise from a second figure that Alice runs into.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock is a verb here, to upset deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter someone is to devastate them emotionally, which is to shock.

clue.text: Rock star finally leaves limo and enters drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of order, so the remaining letters are jumbled
something that leaves departs, so that letter is taken out of the words that follow
finally points to the very end of the word it follows, so only its closing letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of star
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock star stumbles out of a limousine and into a venue, the worse for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' reads as one phrase, but Rock alone is the definition and star only supplies the letter to be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

clue.text: Deplore feeble set of books

parts.note: a lame excuse is a feeble one
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a weak collection of books.
explanation.walkthrough: Set of books suggests a library series, but it is the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament something is to express sorrow or regret over it, close to deploring it.

clue.text: Old-fashioned tailor made veil

indicators.note: a tailor alters and remakes, so these letters are reshaped into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dated-looking veil that a tailor once made.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailor reads as the person who made the veil but is a verb telling us to remake the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval is used informally to mean hopelessly outdated, as if from the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Parcel, for example, chaps found in street

indicators.note: things found in a place are inside it, so the other pieces sit within the street word

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
eg is short for for example
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some men discover a package lying in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Parcel suggests a package, but here it means a portion, as in a parcel of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel can be a portion or piece of something, which is what a segment is.

clue.text: Working hard leaving another pig crackers

indicators.note: crackers means mad, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
a letter that is leaving goes away, so it is taken out of the following words

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard worker walks off, leaving another pig going mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Working hard reads as one phrase, but Working alone is the definition; hard supplies the letter dropped from ANOTHER before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is operating is running or functioning, which is working.

clue.text: Competition's level and tense

parts.note: level and even both mean flat or equal
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A contest that is evenly matched and full of tension.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense is not nervy but the grammar term, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single contest in a sports programme, such as the 100 metres.

clue.text: Swore after former lover cried

indicators.note: after tells us the word for swore is placed behind the word for a former lover

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to swear something is to claim or assert it

explanation.surface: Someone bursts into tears after cursing an old flame.
explanation.walkthrough: Swore suggests cursing, but here it means asserted, as in swearing that something is true.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, so cried in the sense of shouted matches it.

clue.text: My small European birds

parts.note: both are mild exclamations of surprise
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone points out their little flock of European birds.
explanation.walkthrough: My looks like a possessive but is the exclamation, as in 'My, how tall you've grown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are large waterfowl, so they are birds.

clue.text: What you might do with new bra — attempt something audacious

definitions.text: What you might do with new bra
definitions.meaning: first meaning: put on a new garment to check that it fits
second meaning: the idiom for chancing your luck or attempting to deceive

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a literal fitting-room phrase; the second is the British idiom for cheekily seeing what you can get away with.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to test a garment by wearing it and, idiomatically, to make a cheeky attempt to get away with something.

clue.text: Stylish top from emporium on social worker

indicators.note: the top of a word written down is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of emporium
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
ants are social insects that live in colonies and do the work

explanation.surface: A fashionable top bought from a big shop sits on a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: On means LEG from cricket, where the leg side is the on side; a social worker in crosswords is often an ant or bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, a synonym of stylish.

clue.text: What journalist may write about vessel crossing river

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a vessel crossing something lies across it, so the river letter sits inside the vessel word

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A news story about a ship making its way across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a boat, but it is a pot; R goes inside it to give PORT, after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is an account of events, the kind of piece a journalist files.

clue.text: Hoover, perhaps, first bits of irritating dust in here

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word for here

parts.note: present means here, as in answering a register

indicators.note: the first bits of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first letters of irritating and dust

explanation.surface: A vacuum cleaner picks up irritating dust in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover is the vacuum-cleaner brand in Britain, but here it is Herbert Hoover, the 31st US president; perhaps signals an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Hoover was a president of the United States, so he is one example.

clue.text: You might find food in these drawers, Romeo's admitted

definitions.text: You might find food in these

indicators.note: to be admitted is to be let in, so the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: drawers is an old word for underpants
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Food tucked away in a chest of drawers, with Romeo let in on the secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawers suggests furniture, but it is the old word for knickers; R goes inside to give the rooms for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard where food is stored.

clue.text: Abandon terribly red nurse on run

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are put in a disordered arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A flustered, red-faced nurse leaves her post while on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: On means placed after, so R follows the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or relinquish, which is what abandon means.

clue.text: Electrify gate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to thrill or captivate, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a way in, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: en-TRANCE (to enchant) and EN-trance (a doorway).
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to fill with wonder, as electrify does, and an entrance is a way in such as a gate.

clue.text: Lifting bird in grass

indicators.note: in places the bird word inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass on someone is to inform, and informers sing
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Raising a bird up out of the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Lifting is slang for stealing, as in shoplifting; grass here is the verb, to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is informal for taking without permission, as in shoplifting.

clue.text: Shy, unfriendly, tailless marine crustacean

indicators.note: tailless means without its end, so the final letter of that word is cut off

parts.note: to shy is to throw, and a lob is a high throw
stern means severe and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A timid, hostile sea creature that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Shy looks like timid but is the verb to throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is a large clawed crustacean that lives in the sea.

clue.text: More stout? Beer enthrals king

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the beer word holds the other letter within it

parts.note: lager is a type of beer
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone asks for another stout, though the king is hooked on beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the dark beer, which fits the beer surface, but it is the adjective meaning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Larger means bigger in size, and stout describes a heavily built person.

clue.text: Realise that is Victor in pain

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain
ie is short for id est, that is
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone becomes aware that the winner is hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: Realise suggests becoming aware, but here it means bring about, as in realising an ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a goal is to make it happen, which is to achieve it.

clue.text: Single out sailor on land

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to land a prize is to get it

explanation.surface: A sailor is picked out once ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: Land is not ground but the verb to secure, as in landing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To target someone is to select them as the object of attention, which is to single them out.

clue.text: Mountaineer's cold arm possibly uncovered here

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
an arm is one example of a limb

indicators.note: removing the cover from a word strips off its outside letters, leaving only the inner ones

parts.note: the inner letters of here

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's arm is left bare and cold up here.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay; possibly flags that arm is just one example of a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber is someone who scales mountains or rock faces, the same as a mountaineer.

clue.text: Juvenile student in lecture scratching bottom

definitions.note: used as a noun, a young person

indicators.note: in places the student letter inside the shortened word
scratching out the bottom removes the last letter of a down entry

parts.note: to chide is to scold or lecture
L is for learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A young student sitting in a lecture, scratching their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Lecture is the verb, to tell off; in a down clue the bottom is the last letter. An L-plate marks a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile is a young person, the same as a child.

clue.text: Adult permitted wearing the jumper?

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: something being worn is surrounded by clothing, so the permitted word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A grown-up is allowed to put on the woolly jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is British for a sweater, which fits wearing, but the question mark signals a person who jumps, such as a high jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A high jumper or long jumper is one kind of athlete, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Aberdeen terrier holding log

indicators.note: holding means the phrase contains the answer within its letters

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A Scottish terrier clutching a piece of wood in its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Log is the verb, to record, not a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To log data is to record it, which is to enter it in a register.

clue.text: A dead loss in record time

definitions.note: a noun phrase, but it is used like an adjective as in 'he's a dead loss'

indicators.note: in sets the word for record ahead of the other parts in order

parts.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who failed hopelessly, despite setting a record time.
explanation.walkthrough: In is read as itself, followed by EP and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone called a dead loss is hopeless or incompetent, which is what inept means.

clue.text: Decent leg spinning is overlooked

indicators.note: spinning things turn round and round, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decent leg-spinner in cricket fails to be picked.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg spinning suggests cricket, where a leg-spinner is a type of slow bowler, but spinning is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked has been ignored or disregarded, a synonym of neglected.

clue.text: Scare off bloke's cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to frighten off
a gent is a man, informally

explanation.surface: A cleaner chasing a man away.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man; the 's means is, linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, such as washing-up liquid or laundry powder.

clue.text: Nearer cobra, regularly stumble

definitions.note: used as a noun, a slip or blunder

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Getting closer to a cobra, someone keeps tripping over.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumble is the noun here, a slip, rather than the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble can mean a mistake, as in stumbling over words, which is an error.
